@texra-ai/harness/schemas ​

Browser-safe Effect Schemas, derived types, and pure read helpers for @texra-ai/harness.

Guide: Read Views, Transcripts & Renderers and Durable Protocol & Recovery for how views, runtime requests, and approval policies work.

  • Session & run views: SessionView, RunView, TranscriptView, PendingRequest, and pure queries (acceptsFollowUp, attentionOf, sessionActivity, descendantRuns, runActionRefusal).
  • Commands & approvals: RuntimeRequestSchema (RuntimeRequest), RequestDecision, OutcomeSchema, RequestErrorSchema, ApprovalPolicySchema, resolveBypass.
  • Agent definitions & run outcomes: AgentConfigSchema, InlinePersonaSchema, RunEndSchema, RunIdSchema, StartRequestSchema.
  • Settings & trace export: settingsCatalog, configTreeRows, GlobalStateKey, WorkspaceStateKey, TraceDocumentSchema.

acceptsFollowUp ​

Whether a run takes a follow-up at all, the one rule every host reads (it decides whether the composer shows). A run with no follow-up support and a run whose rows this build cannot read take none; a run still going or waiting takes one, as does a stopped native one with saved steps, which a resume continues from its history.

ts
function acceptsFollowUp(run: ReadRunView): boolean

APPROVAL_POLICY_NO_INPUT_DEFAULT ​

The policy a --no-input run falls back to. Deliberately divergent from {@link APPROVAL_POLICY_DEFAULT}: a run that cannot present a prompt denies instead of hanging, and buildCliContext narrows the candidate list to the explicit --approval-policy flag alone — a persisted or env-provided yolo must not silently auto-approve a headless run that nobody is watching. Changing that requires changing headless discipline, not just this constant.

ts
const APPROVAL_POLICY_NO_INPUT_DEFAULT: ApprovalPolicy

Attention ​

What wants this window: the requests it can answer (the badge), and since previous (none without it) the new ones and the runs that ended.

ts
interface Attention<Request> {
  readonly requests: readonly Request[];
  readonly arrived: readonly Request[];
  readonly finished: readonly ReadRunView[];
}

attentionOf ​

The one attention rule every host reads (the extension's badge, reveal and chime, the desktop's dock badge, notifications, and rail): a request wants the user when this window can answer it (not one on a run another process holds or waiting for its run's resume), and a run when its outcome lands.

ts
function attentionOf<View extends ReadSessionView>(
  view: View,
  previous?: ReadSessionView,
): Attention<View['requests'][number]>

blocksCaller ​

Whether a request blocks the tool that opened it: every kind the harness opens does, and a plugin's request as it declares. One that does not leaves its run working; its plugin's decision hook delivers the answer to whichever process holds the run by then, so it stays open across every resume. The folds and the decision door all read this one predicate.

Cancelled ​

Nothing is left to tell the user: they cancelled the operation, or the host has already told them why it did not go through. No refusal notice is needed.

ts
class Cancelled extends Schema.TaggedError<Cancelled>()(
  'Cancelled',
  {},
)

CHATGPT_CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW_SETTING ​

Bounds and copy for the ChatGPT-subscription input budget; unset, each model takes the window the Codex backend grants it.

The stored unit is thousands of tokens, and the key says so. Every budget in play is a round multiple of 1000 (272K, 400K, 872K), so a raw token count is three zeros nobody wants to type and an off-by-1000 typo lands inside the valid range instead of being rejected: 872 entered for 872,000 is a legal 872-token budget that puts every request over the limit, and the failure then names a number the user never meant to set.

ts
const CHATGPT_CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW_SETTING: Readonly<{ readonly configKey: "chatgptCodex.contextWindowK"; readonly tokensPerUnit: 1000; readonly min: 1; readonly max: 872; readonly unitLabel: "K tokens"; readonly description: "Input token budget for ChatGPT-subscription (Codex) routing, in thousands of tokens, mirroring Codex CLI's model_context_window. Unset, each model takes the window the Codex backend grants it (500 for GPT-6.1 Sol, 272 for the others); a value overrides it for every model, up to 872 (872,000 tokens). Automatic compaction may run earlier according to the separate compaction threshold. The model's output budget is added when displaying the total context window. The OpenAI backend enforces the real per-account limit — values above what your subscription allows fail and trigger compaction recovery."; }>

CHILD_RUN_CONCURRENCY_BUDGET_CONFIG_KEY ​

Config key for the per-session child-run concurrency budget.

ts
const CHILD_RUN_CONCURRENCY_BUDGET_CONFIG_KEY: "childRunConcurrencyBudget"

CHILD_RUN_CONCURRENCY_BUDGET_SETTING ​

Bounds, default, and copy for childRunConcurrencyBudget. The value caps the number of live native child model conversations one session runs at once. Shared by the catalog row and the runtime reader so the two cannot disagree about the range.

ts
const CHILD_RUN_CONCURRENCY_BUDGET_SETTING: Readonly<{ readonly auto: 0; readonly defaultValue: 0; readonly min: 0; readonly max: 100; readonly description: "Maximum number of agents one task may run at once in the background; a script's agent() calls also run at most this many at once. 0 (the default) sizes it to this machine's CPU count. Agents beyond the budget wait for a slot to free."; }>

ConfigTarget ​

Where a config write lands. workspace is the project's committable .texra/config.json, which a cloned repository controls; local is this user's private file for the workspace, under the storage root and never in the project; global is the user's file for every workspace.

ts
type ConfigTarget = 'global' | 'workspace' | 'local';

countLines ​

Count the number of lines in a string. Handles both Unix (\n) and Windows (\r\n) line endings. A trailing newline does not count as an extra line.

  • @example countLines('a\nb\nc') // 3 countLines('a\nb\nc\n') // 3 (trailing newline ignored) countLines('') // 0

function countLines(text: string): number

CredentialSwitchSchema ​

The move onto the user's own credential a failed model request offers, decided once by the retry owner (ModelInvoker) from the recorded failure and the route the failed model was bound on. Hosts render it; none of them re-derives it from the error.

ts
const CredentialSwitchSchema: Union<readonly [Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"decline-route">; readonly route: Literals<readonly ["chatgpt-subscription", "xai-subscription", "kimi-code-subscription", "glm-coding-plan-subscription"]>; readonly provider: Literals<readonly ["openai", "anthropic", "google", "xai", "deepseek", "moonshot", "dashscope", "minimax", "glm", "meta", "kimiCode"]>; readonly automatic: Boolean; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"new-key">; readonly provider: Literals<readonly ["openai", "anthropic", "google", "xai", "deepseek", "moonshot", "dashscope", "minimax", "glm", "meta", "kimiCode"]>; }>]>

DEFAULT_AGENT_MODEL ​

Default model used when a new agent run / proposal omits one. Single source of truth shared by the agent config schema, the main-view persisted state, and the progress-view proposal reconstruction — so a change here propagates to all three instead of drifting per call site. DEFAULT_MODELS leads with this model, so it must not be a Gemini id.

FileLocation ​

ts
type FileLocation = typeof FileLocationSchema.Type;

fileLocationAddressPath ​

How a location is addressed in text that leaves the UI — copied run context, follow-up prompts, subagent results. A run-storage location carries the run that owns it, so its /executions/... route resolves without the caller supplying one; every other kind reads as its display path.

ts
function fileLocationAddressPath(location: FileLocation): string

fileLocationDisplayPath ​

How a location reads as a path: workspace and run-storage files by their relative path — that is how the user and the agent's file tools refer to them — and external files by their absolute path, the only path they have.

This doubles as a location's comparable identity: two locations naming the same file agree here, so output-to-base maps key on it.

ts
function fileLocationDisplayPath(location: FileLocation): string

FileLocationSchema ​

Discriminated union of all file location types

ts
const FileLocationSchema: Union<readonly [Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"workspace">; readonly absolutePath: String; readonly relativePath: String; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"runStorage">; readonly absolutePath: String; readonly relativePath: String; readonly runId: brand<String, "RunId">; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"external">; readonly absolutePath: String; }>]>

fileLocationShortDisplayPath ​

Like {@link fileLocationDisplayPath} but collapses an external location to its basename, so a long absolute path (e.g. a run-storage file resolved as external because it sits outside the workspace root) cannot dominate a UI row or a prompt line. The full path stays on absolutePath.

ts
function fileLocationShortDisplayPath(location: FileLocation): string

generateRunId ​

Mint a run id: 12 lowercase hex chars (48 bits of entropy), the first digits of a random UUID, every one of which is random. One of the two minting sites (deriveRunId is the other), so the brand is applied here and nowhere downstream. Any other random id is crypto.randomUUID().

ts
function generateRunId(): RunId

getBasename ​

Extract the base name (filename) from a file path. Handles platform-specific separators (\ on Windows, / on Unix).

  • @example getBasename('/home/user/document.pdf') // returns 'document.pdf' getBasename('C:\Users\file.txt') // returns 'file.txt' getBasename('/path/to/') // returns 'to' getBasename('/') // returns ''
ts
function getBasename(filePath: string | undefined | null): string

const GlobalStateKey: Readonly<{ readonly MEMORY_ENABLED: "memory.enabled"; readonly SCRIPT_ONLY: "codeMode.scriptOnly"; readonly ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_KILL: "allowOrchestratorKill"; readonly DETACH_SUBAGENTS_ON_STOP: "detachSubagentsOnStop"; readonly MODEL_SELECTION: "modelSelection"; readonly HELPER_MODEL: "helperModel"; readonly REASONING_LEVELS: "reasoningLevels"; readonly CUSTOM_AGENT_DIR: "customAgentDir"; readonly GLM_CODING_PLAN: "glm.codingPlan"; readonly KIMI_CODE_PREFER: "kimiCode.prefer"; readonly WEBSOCKET_OPENAI: "websocket.openai"; readonly DISABLED_TOOLS: "tools.disabled"; readonly MCP_REVISION_KEY: "mcp.revisionKey"; readonly INSTALLED_PLUGINS: "plugins.installed"; readonly ACTIVE_TEAM_ID: "onboarding.defaultTeamId"; }>

GOAL_MAX_COST_SETTING ​

Bounds, default, and copy for goal.maxCostUsd: what a goal's rounds may spend before it pauses instead of starting another round, and 0 disables the cap. Read when the goal launches, into its script. Shared by the catalog row and the goal launch so the two cannot disagree about the range.

ts
const GOAL_MAX_COST_SETTING: Readonly<{ readonly configKey: "goal.maxCostUsd"; readonly defaultValue: 5; readonly min: 0; readonly max: 10000; readonly description: "Spend in US dollars, across its rounds, at which an autonomous goal pauses instead of starting another round. Raise it, then run the goal again to continue. Set to 0 to remove the cap (not recommended with auto-approve on your own API key)."; }>

GOAL_STRATEGY_SETTING ​

Default and copy for goal.strategy: the script module whose goal export a plan run as a goal calls. The default is the goal plugin's own module; a scriptModules entry of any plugin that is on may replace it. Read when the goal launches.

ts
const GOAL_STRATEGY_SETTING: Readonly<{ readonly configKey: "goal.strategy"; readonly defaultValue: "builtIn:goal"; readonly description: "The script module a plan run as a goal runs, by its import specifier (`builtIn:<module>`): its `goal(objective, { maxCostUsd })` export decides the rounds, what context each starts from and when to stop, and resolves to the goal's result. Defaults to the goal plugin's own module."; }>

GoalResultSchema ​

A goal's result: what its strategy, the goal export of the script module the goal.strategy setting names, returns, and so the structured output its run ends with. completed when a round verified the objective, paused with the reason otherwise. A pause is a result, not a waiting run: work continues through a new goal or a new turn.

ts
const GoalResultSchema: Union<readonly [Struct<{ readonly rounds: Int; readonly spent: Finite; readonly report: String; readonly outcome: Literal<"completed">; }>, Struct<{ readonly rounds: Int; readonly spent: Finite; readonly report: String; readonly outcome: Literal<"paused">; readonly pause: Union<readonly [Struct<{ readonly reason: Literal<"needs_user">; }>, Struct<{ readonly reason: Literal<"round_failed">; readonly error: Struct<{ readonly name: String; readonly message: String; }>; }>, Struct<{ readonly reason: Literal<"no_verdict">; readonly response: String; }>, Struct<{ readonly reason: Literal<"spend_cap">; readonly maxCostUsd: Finite; }>]>; }>]>

HARNESS_INSTRUCTION_KEY ​

The instruction keys the harness itself emits as {@link RequestShowInstructionPayload.key}. A key names the notice for the host's "never remind again" state; an embedder decides what each of these offers beside the message (TeXRA: the buttons that set a key or open a guide). An embedder's own notices use keys of their own.

ts
const HARNESS_INSTRUCTION_KEY: { readonly MISSING_API_KEY: "missingApiKey"; readonly MODEL_NOT_RECOGNIZED: "modelNotRecognized"; readonly RESUME_REFUSED: "resumeRefused"; }

HarnessInstructionKey ​

ts
type HarnessInstructionKey =
  (typeof HARNESS_INSTRUCTION_KEY)[keyof typeof HARNESS_INSTRUCTION_KEY];

HookEvent ​

ts
type HookEvent = typeof HookEventSchema.Type;

HumanInputDecision ​

Whether a human-input request may be shown, or why it settles denied.

ts
type HumanInputDecision =
  | 'present'
  | {
      readonly deny: 'yolo-no-human' | 'policy' | 'unpresentable';
    };

InlinePersona ​

An inline persona as an embedder writes it (before defaults).

ts
type InlinePersona = typeof InlinePersonaSchema.Encoded;

InlinePersonaSchema ​

A persona an embedder passes inline (StartInput.agent) instead of a file: the same definition with nothing a file alone can mean. It has no bundled original and no plugin's block (a task is its plugin's recipe); each is refused as an unrecognized key.

ts
const InlinePersonaSchema: Struct<{ readonly description: optional<String>; readonly name: Trim; readonly prompt: optional<String>; readonly temperature: optional<Number>; readonly tools: optional<$Array<String>>; }>

InputHistoryRecord ​

ts
type InputHistoryRecord = typeof InputHistoryRecordSchema.Type;

InstalledPluginSchema ​

One installed plugin, persisted as a row of the plugins.installed state: the one install record every host reads and writes (a CLI's plugin command, a settings page). The plugin keeps its own manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json or .codex-plugin/plugin.json); this row is where it lives, whether it is enabled, the trust given to it, and what stands in for a manifest the plugin does not have (the marketplace entry's skill directories, version and description).

name takes the skill-name grammar, which also makes it a safe single path segment for the managed plugins/<name> directory. commit is set exactly when the harness fetched the plugin with git and owns its directory; a local plugin is referenced in place and has none.

ts
const InstalledPluginSchema: Struct<{ readonly name: decodeTo<String, String, never, never>; readonly source: String; readonly ref: optional<String>; readonly commit: optional<String>; readonly path: String; readonly skills: $Array<String>; readonly version: optional<String>; readonly description: optional<String>; readonly enabled: Boolean; readonly trust: optional<Struct<{ readonly version: NullOr<String>; readonly digest: String; }>>; }>

Invalid ​

The request could not be parsed: a bridge's answer, never the runtime's.

ts
class Invalid extends Schema.TaggedError<Invalid>()('Invalid', {
  reason: Schema.String,
})

isEmptyUsage ​

Whether usage stats are all zeros (effectively empty).

ts
function isEmptyUsage(usage: TokenUsageStats): boolean

isInFlightPhase ​

ts
function isInFlightPhase(
  phase: RunLifecycleStatus | undefined,
): boolean

isModelOptionAvailable ​

Whether an option row can be run as shipped: readModelOptions already resolved the access question, so a caller only has to read its verdict. Lives with the kind so delegation's model list and the CLI's picker can never drift apart on what "available" means.

ts
function isModelOptionAvailable(model: {
  readonly availability?: ModelAvailabilityKind;
}): boolean

isPackagedAgentSource ​

True for the sources whose definitions are read in place and are not the user's to edit: the bundled one, and an installed plugin's. Every surface that offers to open one presents it read-only and points edits at the custom copy; the extension additionally registers the bundled directories writable: false for its file tools.

ts
function isPackagedAgentSource(source: AgentSource): boolean

isRunId ​

Whether a string is a run id, as {@link RunIdSchema} reads it.

ts
const isRunId: <I>(input: I) => input is I & string & Brand<"RunId">

isTaskConfig ​

Whether the run is a task (an agent carrying a plugin's block, run on its recipe): its value and its children's spend are its output, its end its record; it resumes from its checkpoint, its opening rebuilt.

isTerminalOutcomePhase ​

Whether a RunPhase is one of the three terminal outcome phases (COMPLETED | CANCELLED | FAILED). This is the single enumeration of that set — hosts must consume it rather than hand-rolling their own.

ts
function isTerminalOutcomePhase(
  phase: RunLifecycleStatus | undefined,
): phase is RunOutcome

isTranscriptSettlementPhase ​

Whether transcript content is settled for the current turn.

ts
function isTranscriptSettlementPhase(
  phase: RunLifecycleStatus | undefined,
): boolean

MODEL_AVAILABILITY_STATUS ​

What a kind means: whether a run can use the model, and whether the block is a missing key (a surface's words for each kind are the app's). Declared once here, next to the kind, so the answer is carried on the wire as the kind alone and every host reads the same table instead of pre-fanned fields.

Written with as const satisfies so each available literal survives for computeModelOptions's derivation of the unavailable kinds, while a missing or misshapen kind is still a compile error, and frozen to the depth it is read at: the table crosses into every host that decides whether a model can run, and readonly is compile-time only.

ts
const MODEL_AVAILABILITY_STATUS: { readonly 'provider-key': { readonly available: true; readonly requiresKey: false; }; readonly 'missing-key': { readonly available: false; readonly requiresKey: true; }; readonly 'key-unreadable': { readonly available: false; readonly requiresKey: false; }; readonly 'subscription-access': { readonly available: true; readonly requiresKey: false; }; readonly 'xai-subscription-access': { readonly available: true; readonly requiresKey: false; }; readonly retired: { readonly available: false; readonly requiresKey: false; }; readonly unserved: { readonly available: false; readonly requiresKey: false; }; readonly 'unknown-model': { readonly available: false; readonly requiresKey: false; }; }

MODEL_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD_SETTING ​

Bounds, default, and copy for model.compactionThresholdPercent. The value is the share of the model's context window that triggers automatic compaction, and 0 disables it. Shared by the catalog row and the runtime reader so the two cannot disagree about the range.

ts
const MODEL_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD_SETTING: Readonly<{ readonly configKey: "model.compactionThresholdPercent"; readonly defaultValue: 75; readonly min: 0; readonly max: 100; readonly description: "When the conversation reaches this percentage of the model's context limit, earlier messages are summarized automatically to free up space. Lower values trigger summarization sooner. Set to 0 to disable."; }>

MODEL_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS_SETTING ​

Bounds, default, and copy for model.retry.maxAttempts. The value is the number of automatic retries after the initial model request. Shared by the catalog row's schema and its copy so the two cannot disagree about the range.

ts
const MODEL_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS_SETTING: Readonly<{ readonly configKey: "model.retry.maxAttempts"; readonly defaultValue: 2; readonly min: 0; readonly max: 5; readonly description: "Additional automatic retries after the initial model request (0–5). A resumed request keeps the retries it already used."; }>

ReadonlyDeep ​

A runtime value as a host or an embedder holds it: read-only all the way down, every map, array, and record included. The value itself is not copied (the fold publishes immutable levels); the type is what keeps a write from reaching it. A primitive stays itself, so a branded id (a RunId) is still that id.

ts
type ReadonlyDeep<T> = T extends
  | string
  | number
  | boolean
  | bigint
  | symbol
  | null
  | undefined
  | ((...args: never[]) => unknown)
  ? T
  : T extends ReadonlyMap<infer K, infer V>
    ? ReadonlyMap<K, ReadonlyDeep<V>>
    : T extends ReadonlySet<infer V>
      ? ReadonlySet<ReadonlyDeep<V>>
      : T extends readonly (infer E)[]
        ? readonly ReadonlyDeep<E>[]
        : T extends object
          ? { readonly [P in keyof T]: ReadonlyDeep<T[P]> }
          : T;

readTraceFacts ​

A parsed trace with each plugin fact checked as the store checks it, against the harness's built-in fact kind (the goal's plan) and the app's plugin fact kinds (appFactKinds). A fact at another version than its kind's, or whose value the kind's schema rejects, throws, naming it, as does a retired built-in fact no current plugin owns; one whose plugin this build lacks is kept as written, marked unavailable, as the store reads it.

ts
function readTraceFacts(
  document: TraceDocument,
  appFactKinds: readonly TraceFactKind[],
): TraceDocument

Whether this window can answer a pending request: the one rule the host's attention badge and the request card both read, matching what SessionRequests.decide accepts. type ResponseCut = typeof ResponseCutSchema.Type;

ResumeRefusal ​

One reason a resume is refused ({@link ResumeRefusalSchema}).

ts
type ResumeRefusal = typeof ResumeRefusalSchema.Type;

ResumeRefusalSchema ​

Why a persisted run is not continued here: the one answer a resume, a message to a run with no loop here, a run's records and its view give. finished (nothing left to continue from), blocked ({@link ResumeBlockedSchema}), unusableCheckpoint (its saved state is there but cannot be continued: never finished, which would say it ended normally), earlierBuild (an earlier build wrote its rows), pluginUnavailable (it holds a fact of plugin, which this process does not load, cause the fact's reason: it continues once a process loads it), or notResumable (it was deleted, or its input is closed).

ts
const ResumeRefusalSchema: Union<readonly [Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"finished">; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"blocked">; readonly blocker: Literals<readonly ["agentMissing", "pluginOff", "pluginUntrusted"]>; readonly name: String; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"unusableCheckpoint">; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"earlierBuild">; readonly cause: String; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"pluginUnavailable">; readonly plugin: String; readonly cause: String; }>, Struct<{ readonly kind: Literal<"notResumable">; }>]>

RetryApprovalDecision ​

ts
type RetryApprovalDecision =
  | 'present'
  | {
      readonly deny: 'yolo-retry' | 'credential' | 'policy' | 'unpresentable';
    };

RetryPermission ​

ts
type RetryPermission = typeof RetryPermissionSchema.Type;

rollupOf ​

What children and their descendants count toward a parent's rollup: the view's count over the run tree (each child's own rollup below it), and the dispatch card's over the tree it lists (below recurses through the children it lists instead). A child waiting between turns (held) or paused, nothing asked of the user, has delivered its turn: it counts as finished, not running.

ts
function rollupOf(
  children: readonly ReadRunView[],
  below = (child: ReadRunView) => child.rollup,
): ReadRunView['rollup']

RUN_LIFECYCLE_READY ​

Wire-level lifecycle status of a run with no lifecycle recorded yet. as const is load-bearing: a bare const gives a widening literal type, which widens back to string inside an object literal.

ts
const RUN_LIFECYCLE_READY: "ready"

RUN_OUTCOME ​

Canonical terminal outcome of an agent run — the single fact "how did this run end", decided exactly once at the run-lifecycle boundary. Current production writers use these values for terminal run, group-end, and run state.

cancelled is a sibling of failed, never folded into it — a user stop is not an error. This is the triad ResultEvent.outcome carries.

ts
const RUN_OUTCOME: { readonly COMPLETED: "completed"; readonly CANCELLED: "cancelled"; readonly FAILED: "failed"; }

RUN_PHASE ​

The live phase vocabulary. Membership questions are answered by the predicates isInFlightPhase and isTerminalOutcomePhase; whether a run is working right now is the session view's working.

ts
const RUN_PHASE: { readonly RUNNING: "running"; readonly WAITING: "waiting"; readonly COMPLETED: "completed"; readonly CANCELLED: "cancelled"; readonly FAILED: "failed"; }

Every key of the status table, the enum RunView.statusKey holds.

RunEndSchema ​

A run's terminal result as every reader sees it. error is present only on a failed outcome; usage once a round recorded usage, including on failures. Cost is usage.totalCost and nothing else. settingsCatalog ​

The harness's rows, then rows (an app's own, its plugins' included), stored under namespace. A key declared twice is a defect and throws, and so does a defaults key that names no harness row.

ts
function settingsCatalog(options: {
  readonly namespace: string;
  readonly rows: readonly StateSettingEntry[];
  /** The app's own defaults for harness rows, by key: the value an absent
   *  key reads as (the helper model, which the harness leaves unset). */
  readonly defaults?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}): SettingsCatalog

SettingsCatalog ​

One settings catalog: its rows and the lookups the stores read from them.

ts
interface SettingsCatalog {
  /** The app's prefix on every stored key (`texra`): the config and state
   *  stores write a row's relative key as `<namespace>.<key>`. */
  readonly namespace: string;
  /** Every row, in catalog order. */
  readonly rows: readonly StateSettingEntry[];
  /** Look up any row, config-file-backed or state-backed, by its key. */
  readonly byKey: (key: string) => StateSettingEntry | undefined;
  /** Look up a row by its stored key, as a store lists it. */
  readonly byStoredKey: (storedKey: string) => StateSettingEntry | undefined;
  /**
   * A fresh copy of a config-file-backed row's default, or `undefined` for a
   * key no such row owns: what every `ConfigProvider` answers for an absent
   * key. Parsed defaults are memoized
   * because this is on the read path of every absent setting; object values
   * are cloned so a caller cannot mutate the catalog's own default.
   */
  readonly configDefault: (key: string) => unknown;
}

SettingStore ​

Storage slot a setting is read from / written to. repoState is shared by every checkout of one git repository (keyed by its root in the global database), so a repository has one value on every host and in every worktree.

ts
type SettingStore =
  | 'config'
  | 'workspaceState'
  | 'repoState'
  | 'globalState';

splitContentLines ​

Normalize line endings and split into content lines. A trailing newline does not produce a phantom empty element.

  • @example splitContentLines('a\nb\nc') // ['a', 'b', 'c'] splitContentLines('a\nb\nc\n') // ['a', 'b', 'c'] splitContentLines('') // []

function splitContentLines(text: string): string[]

StartRequestSchema ​

A start as data: all of StartInput but the run's own tools. Either an agent (a name from the agent directories, or a persona written inline, which the run stores so a resume needs no file) and the instruction to give it, or config, a complete configuration an application host has already resolved. A host sends it to a service as it is.

StateSettingEntry ​

ts
interface StateSettingEntry {
  /** The row's key, relative to its catalog's namespace (`memory.enabled`),
   *  which the stores add (`<namespace>.memory.enabled`). */
  readonly key: string;
  /**
   * The row's schema, carrying both validation and the decoding default
   * applied when the key is absent: decoding `undefined` yields that default.
   */
  readonly schema: Schema.Codec<unknown, unknown>;
  /** Short label for compact settings UIs; falls back to the stripped key. */
  readonly title?: string;
  /** Human-readable description, shared across every host that renders it. */
  readonly description?: string;
  /** Grouping label for settings UIs. Required once a UI renders the row. */
  readonly category?: string;
  /** Where the value is stored, the same on every host. */
  readonly slot: SettingStore;
  /** Config-backed target, workspace when omitted; `global`/`local` skip the project file. */
  readonly configTarget?: 'global' | 'workspace' | 'local';
  /**
   * A `global` row a project file may still switch off: its project value
   * counts unless it is `true`, so a repository can opt out (telemetry) but
   * never opt in. A malformed project value counts too, and fails closed.
   */
  readonly projectMayOptOut?: true;
  /**
   * Per-value descriptions for an enum setting, aligned 1:1 with the schema's
   * enum options (a host's settings UI derives them). The option *values* are
   * derived from the schema, not restated here.
   */
  readonly enumDescriptions?: readonly string[];
  /** Display labels for enum options, aligned 1:1 with the schema options. */
  readonly enumLabels?: readonly string[];
}

stripControlCharacters ​

Replace every C0/C1 control character (tab and newline included) with replacement, so untrusted text cannot inject terminal escapes.

ts
function stripControlCharacters(text: string, replacement = ''): string

SUBSCRIPTION_AUTH_PROVIDERS ​

The subscription providers, as a settings view signs in and out of them: the one spelling of a provider id everywhere. What a person calls each subscription and its sign-in is an app's copy; the harness's own failure text names a subscription by the provider it bills.

ts
const SUBSCRIPTION_AUTH_PROVIDERS: readonly ["chatgpt", "grok"]

SubscriptionAuthProvider ​

ts
type SubscriptionAuthProvider =
  (typeof SUBSCRIPTION_AUTH_PROVIDERS)[number];

Accumulates usage stats from an iterable into a single total. The route and plan are kept when every nonempty item names the same one.

  items: Iterable<TokenUsageStats>,
): TokenUsageStats

toErrorMessage ​

Normalize any thrown value into a user-friendly error message string: the error's own message, then the messages down its cause chain (and an AggregateError's members), each once, joined with : . A wrapper whose sentence already embeds its cause's message adds nothing, and a wrapper with a fixed sentence no longer hides the failure under it.

ts
function toErrorMessage(err: unknown): string

toJsonValue ​

A value as a stored row keeps it: what JSON.stringify writes, read back. The boundary where an arbitrary value enters a persisted field.

ts
const toJsonValue: (value: unknown) => Json

type TokenUsageStats = typeof TokenUsageStatsSchema.Type;

TraceDocumentSchema ​

One finished run as a static viewer replays it: the run aggregate's own display events in commit order, the same rows the live plane delivers to a subscriber. Nothing is projected on the way out and nothing is reconstructed on the way in.

The export authors four facts rather than copying them (assembleTrace): no owner, no parent, no checkpoint and no follow-up support, because an exported file has no producer, no siblings and no writable host.

TraceFactKind ​

A plugin row kind as an imported trace reads it: a Plugin fact kind.

ts
interface TraceFactKind {
  readonly plugin: string;
  readonly kind: string;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly schema: Schema.Codec<unknown, unknown>;
}

TranscriptView ​

A stream's transcript slice: what hosts paint.

ts
type TranscriptView = RunView['transcript'];

truncateSummary ​

Collapse whitespace first, then truncate to a fixed-width one-line summary.

ts
function truncateSummary(text: string, maxLength: number): string

truncateWithEllipsis ​

Truncate a string to maxLen grapheme clusters with a trailing ellipsis (…). Returns the original string unchanged if it fits within the limit.

Uses Intl.Segmenter so multi-codepoint graphemes (ZWJ emoji sequences like 👨‍👩‍👧, combining diacritics, …) are counted and cut as single units — no split surrogates and no torn emoji.

  • @example truncateWithEllipsis('short', 60) // 'short' truncateWithEllipsis('a very long text', 10) // 'a very lo…'
ts
function truncateWithEllipsis(text: string, maxLen: number): string
